text.hi: Discriminant (D = b² - 4ac) batata hai ki quadratic equation ke roots kis type ke honge - real aur distinct, real aur equal, ya phir imaginary. Yeh concept bahut important hai!
text.en: Discriminant (D = b² - 4ac) batata hai ki quadratic equation ke roots kis type ke honge - real aur distinct, real aur equal, ya phir imaginary. Yeh concept bahut important hai!

content.hi:
What is Discriminant?
Discriminant quadratic formula ka woh part hai jo roots ki nature decide karta hai.
• Discriminant = D = b² - 4ac
• D > 0 → Two distinct real roots
• D = 0 → Two equal real roots (ek hi root repeat hota hai)
• D < 0 → No real roots (imaginary/complex roots)
• D perfect square hone par roots rational hote hain

💡 Remember: Discriminant sirf D = b² - 4ac hai. Iski value se sab kuch pata chalta hai!

content.hi:
Nature of Roots based on Discriminant
D > 0 → Real & Distinct | D = 0 → Real & Equal | D < 0 → No Real Roots
Yeh teen conditions roots ki nature determine karti hain. Har condition ke liye graph alag alag hota hai.
Example: x²-4x+4=0 mein D=16-16=0, so real and equal roots (x=2,2)

content.hi:
Graphical Interpretation
Parabola (quadratic graph) ka x-axis se relation:
• D > 0 → Parabola x-axis ko do alag points par cut karta hai (2 distinct roots)
• D = 0 → Parabola x-axis ko exactly ek point par touch karta hai (1 repeated root)
• D < 0 → Parabola x-axis ko kabhi nahi touch karta (no real roots)
